14    Senator Hinchey, mourning the death of Ronald F. 

15    Lipton, distinguished citizen, devoted public 

16    servant, and cherished member of his community.

17                 ACTING PRESIDENT BAILEY:   Senator 

18    Hinchey on the resolution.

19                 SENATOR HINCHEY:   Thank you, 

20    Mr. President.  

21                 I rise today to honor the 

22    extraordinary legacy of a beloved Greene County 

23    community member and friend, Ron Lipton, who 

24    passed away on January 22nd this year at the age 

25    of 85.  


                                                                5991

 1                 Ron believed that each of us must 

 2    actively work to change the world for the better, 

 3    starting right in our own communities, and he 

 4    lived that belief to its fullest.  He lived 

 5    through and witnessed some of the most tumultuous 

 6    times of social and political upheaval of the 

 7    past century.  Instead of turning to apathy and 

 8    cynicism, he looked to the strongest force for 

 9    good that he knew, people.  

10                 In each community that was lucky 

11    enough to count Ron as a resident, he learned the 

12    local issues, brought people together, and 

13    advocated for real commonsense solutions that 

14    would actually make a difference in people's 

15    lives.  

16                 As a young man, he committed himself 

17    to global humanitarian service, through the 

18    international aid organization Care, in the early 

19    1970s.  When he returned to the U.S., Ron 

20    ventured to California, serving as an advisor to 

21    then Governor Jerry Brown, during a pivotal 

22    moment in environmental and economic reform.  

23                 In 2006, Ron relocated to Lexington, 

24    in Greene County, for his retirement.  And it 

25    should be said that it says a lot about a person 


                                                                5992

 1    who chooses to move to a beautiful-but-can-be- 

 2    fairly-challenging area like the Mountain Top 

 3    upon retirement.  

 4                 But oh, how lucky we were.  What 

 5    might have been a period of rest and tranquility 

 6    instead became a vibrant new chapter of active 

 7    community involvement on the mountain.  He served 

 8    with distinction as the cochair of the Lexington 

 9    Town Democratic Committee and was an active 

10    member of the Mountain Top Progressives, an 

11    organization he helped found and lead as a forum 

12    for connection and activism across the rural 

13    community that shared Mountain Top towns.  

14                 Ron had an insatiable drive to right 

15    wrongs and better the lives of those around him.  

16    Over the years, my team and I worked with Ron on 

17    a number of occasions.  Always fighting for the 

18    well-being of his neighbors, Ron never just 

19    brought us grievances, he worked with us on 

20    solutions.  In fact, one of my favorite topics to 

21    discuss with Ron was energy policy, an area he 

22    focused on during his tenure with Governor Jerry 

23    Brown.  

24                 He was advocating to me for 

25    PSC reform and utility oversight well before it 


                                                                5993

 1    was in our everyday lexicon.  And our bill to 

 2    change the makeup of the PSC and require 

 3    affordability in all proceedings -- which has 

 4    already passed this chamber -- was written in 

 5    partnership with Ron and his wisdom.

 6                 We all know that in this job one of 

 7    the best parts is meeting the people that would 

 8    otherwise probably never cross our path.  For me, 

 9    one of those incredibly special people was 

10    Ron Lipton.  

11                 I'll spare the whole story, but my 

12    first meeting with Ron almost never happened.  

13    You see, we were scheduled to meet at Maggie's 

14    Crooked Cafe in Tannersville.  However, that part 

15    of town had exactly zero cell service.  Both Ron 

16    and I waited for over an hour for the other to 

17    show up, not knowing that the other was just 

18    sitting just a few feet away, one inside and one 

19    outside.  

20                 It was a quick lesson for me on the 

21    lack of critical infrastructure across our rural 

22    communities.

23                 At the last moment, Ron and I did 

24    find each other, and thank God we did.  That 

25    meeting started a wonderful friendship filled 


                                                                5994

 1    with life lessons to me from Ron.  I was in awe 

 2    of his travels, his stories, his energy and his 

 3    moral clarity that never wavered.  

 4                 Those of us lucky enough to have 

 5    known Ron Lipton will forever miss the example he 

 6    set in his community-minded leadership.  And of 

 7    course, his persistence.  My one regret is that I 

 8    never made it with him to the Bronx Zoo, but I 

 9    promise that I will get there in his honor.  

10                 Joining us in the gallery today are 

11    friends of Ron who have become family.  We 

12    remember Ron today in this chamber but will carry 

13    his lessons, his humor, his passion and his 

14    memory with us forever.  

15                 I proudly vote aye on this 

16    resolution and look forward to honoring Ron and 

17    his memory in the years to come.

18                 Thank you.

25                 Today this resolution recognizes 


                                                                5996

 1    that May of this year is Cystic Fibrosis 

 2    Awareness Month.  

 3                 Cystic fibrosis is a rather 

 4    devastating genetic disease that affects the 

 5    lungs, digestive system and other vital organs.  

 6    It affects 1600 New Yorkers and of course tens of 

 7    thousands of families across the country.  

 8                 Today we are joined by one of those 

 9    individuals, Kellen McHale, who is here in -- 

10    stand up, please, Kellen, if you would.  He 

11    attends Lynnwood Academy in Guilderland, and he 

12    is one of those who knows what it's like to daily 

13    live and go through hours of treatment, 

14    medications and therapies simply to breathe, eat 

15    and stay healthy.  

16                 However, he has shown, as well as so 

17    many others with this disease, extraordinary 

18    resilience, courage, and hope.  

19                 And because of decades of research 

20    and advocacy, as well as innovation, today those 

21    with CF, or cystic fibrosis, live longer, fuller 

22    lives than ever before.  And treatments that were 

23    unimaginable just a generation ago are really 

24    allowing patients to attend school, play 

25    baseball, as Kellen does, build careers, raise 


                                                                5997

 1    families, and pursue multiple dreams.  

 2                 That's why awareness is so essential 

 3    for this disease, as is early diagnosis with 

 4    newborn screening, continued investments in 

 5    research.  And all, combined, can make a 

 6    life-changing difference here for these families 

 7    and individuals.  

 8                 It is important that here in 

 9    New York we continue to support world-class 

10    treatment centers and support our dedicated 

11    health professionals as well as the parents, the 

12    caregivers and all the loved ones who shoulder 

13    the burden behind the scenes and help young 

14    people like Kellen navigate the healthcare system 

15    through their unwavering support, as his mom and 

16    granddad and more are here to support him.

17                 As lawmakers we do have that 

18    responsibility to make sure that we continue to 

19    provide quality access to affordable care, to 

20    strengthen biomedical research, and ensure that 

21    New Yorkers living with CF have the opportunity 

22    to live these longer, healthier lives through 

23    this advancement of medical progress.

24                 So today, on behalf of myself as 

25    well as Senator Ashby, who is a friend of the
